description: List the dated events ahead that could move a stock: earnings, FDA decisions, trial readouts, lockups, debt maturities and votes, each with how firm the date is.
suggested_questions: Build a catalyst calendar for Viking Therapeutics (VKTX) for the next 12 months.
Build a catalyst calendar for Rocket Lab (RKLB) for the next 12 months.
Build a catalyst calendar for CoreWeave (CRWV) for the next 12 months.
skill:
Where catalyst dates live:
- Earnings and investor days: the IR events calendar, the latest earnings release, exchange notices. A date the
  company has announced is confirmed; a date inferred from last year's pattern is estimated.
- Conferences: the IR site's events list and conference organisers' agendas.
- Healthcare: FDA PDUFA goal dates as disclosed by the company, FDA advisory committee calendars (fda.gov), EMA CHMP
  meeting dates, ClinicalTrials.gov (primary completion date and its history of changes; a pushed date is itself a
  signal), medical meeting abstract deadlines and late-breaker sessions.
- Capital markets: lockup expiry terms in the IPO prospectus (424B4) or follow-on filings, debt maturities in the debt
  footnote and indentures, convertible note conversion or put dates, redemption notices, buyback authorisation
  expiries.
- Governance: annual meeting and record dates in the DEF 14A, special meetings, proxy contest deadlines, spin-off
  record and distribution dates in Form 10 filings.
- Index changes: S&P Dow Jones Indices and FTSE Russell announcements, the Russell reconstitution calendar.
- Legal and regulatory: court calendars and dockets (CourtListener, PACER summaries in filings), ITC investigation
  target dates, agency comment deadlines, contract award dates in procurement notices.
- Products: launch dates the company announced, regulatory clearances pending, auto and device certification filings.

What terms mean:
- certainty: confirmed (the organiser or company published the date), company_guided (the company gave a window such
  as "second half"), statutory (fixed by a published rule or contract term), estimated (inferred from a pattern).
- why_it_matters: one line on what could move, stated as a fact about the event, not a forecast.

Pitfalls: a stale calendar entry for an event already held, a trial date on the registry that the company has since
revised, a conference appearance confused with an earnings date. Pending-merger approvals are tracked by the deal
approval tracker.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: Catalyst calendar for one listed company.

key.description: Stable lowercase identifier for this item, built from fixed parts joined by underscores (e.g. us_doj_hsr, first_lien_term_loan_2031, q3_2026_earnings). The same item gets the same key in every run.

expected_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD when a day is published.

date_text.description: The date as published, e.g. 2026-12-03, Q1 2027, second half of 2027.

description.description: The event, with the product, instrument or case it concerns.

why_it_matters.description: One line on what could move, stated as fact.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

date_changes.description: Catalyst dates that moved in the last six months.

items.description: Catalyst dates that moved in the last six months.

event_key.description: Key of the event in events.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

checked_no_finding.description: Searches that came back empty, so a gap is a verified absence rather than a skipped check.

items.description: Searches that came back empty, so a gap is a verified absence rather than a skipped check.

result.description: What came back, e.g. no filing found, register shows no case.
